front: Formula: Expected return and variance with scenarios
back:
E(R) = Σ pi Ri
Var(R) = Σ pi (Ri − E(R))²

Use: Returns given per state of the economy with probabilities.
Trap: Weights are the probabilities – no T − 1 here.

Not on the formula sheet – learn it by heart.

U = E(R) − (γ/2) × Var(R)

Use: Ranking investments for a risk-averse investor.
Trap: Use the variance, not the volatility.

Not on the formula sheet – learn it by heart.

Cov(Ri, Rj) = (1/(T − 1)) Σ (Ri,t − R̄i)(Rj,t − R̄j)
scenarios: Σ ps (Ri,s − E(Ri))(Rj,s − E(Rj))

Use: How two returns move together (only the sign is easy to read).
Trap: Historical data: T − 1, like the variance.

Not on the formula sheet – learn it by heart.

ρi,j = Cov(Ri, Rj) / (σi σj)   ⟺   Cov = ρ σi σj

Use: Strength of comovement on a scale from −1 to +1.
Trap: Same sign as the covariance.

Not on the formula sheet – learn it by heart.

βj,M = Cov(Rj, RM) / Var(RM) = ρj,M × σj / σM

Use: How much a stock moves when the market (or another asset) moves by 1%.
Trap: Divide by the variance of the asset that does the moving.

E(Rp) = x1 E(R1) + x2 E(R2),   x1 + x2 = 1

Use: Expected return of any portfolio: a plain weighted average.
Trap: Weights on own money, not on the total position.

σp² = x1² σ1² + x2² σ2² + 2 x1 x2 ρ12 σ1 σ2

Use: Risk of a two-asset portfolio.
Trap: Never forget the cross term; a short position flips its sign.

ρ = +1: σp = x1 σ1 + x2 σ2
ρ < 1: σp < x1 σ1 + x2 σ2
ρ = −1: σp = |x1 σ1 − x2 σ2|

Use: Quick check of how much diversification a pair offers.

Not on the formula sheet – learn it by heart.
